title: rAF Timestamp Relativeness Mismatch
body:
As specified right now, `requestAnimationFrame`'s callback is invoked with an absolute timestamp (the __unsafe shared current time__), whereas `performance.now` returns a timestamp that is relative to `performance.timeOrigin`.

This does not match with observed implementation practice.

In all tested browsers (Firefox v100.0; Chrome v101.0.4951.64; Edge v101.0.1210.47; Opera v86.0.4363.59; Safari v15.4), the passed timestamp is relative to `performance.timeOrigin`, as can be seen by comparing it to `performance.now()`.

JS sample to verify:
```js
;{
        let start = performance.now();
        requestAnimationFrame(end =>
                console.log("rAF timestamp most likely " + (end - performance.timeOrigin - start < -200 ? "relative" : "absolute")
        ))
}
```

Expected log output as currently specified would be `rAF timestamp most likely absolute`. In all tested browsers, the log output was `rAF timestamp most likely relative`.

## Relevant steps

[§ 8.1.6.3 "Processing model"](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/webappapis.html#event-loop-processing-model):

> 5. Let *now* be the __unsafe shared current time__. [HRT]

This variable is not further modified.

> 13. For each __fully active__ `Document` in *docs*, __run the animation frame callbacks__ for that `Document`, passing in *now* as the timestamp.

This links to [§ 8.11's **run the animation frame callbacks**](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/imagebitmap-and-animations.html#run-the-animation-frame-callbacks) algorithm.

This algorithm invokes the callbacks as follows:

> __Invoke__ *callback*, passing *now* as the only argument, and if an exception is thrown, report the exception.

Note that the *now* passed into the *callback* here is still the __unsafe shared current time__.


If we examine the specification of `performance.now` in [HRT](https://w3c.github.io/hr-time/), we find that it returns the result of __relative high resolution time__ instead, which is relativized to the result of __get time origin timestamp__ (which is exposed via `performance.timeOrigin`).

## Further notes

As some external algorithms are called with the *now* timestamp, I am not sure what the correct specification fix for this would be.

In particular, the IntersectionObserver spec also passes the timestamp to JavaScript unchanged (see step 2.14 of the [update intersection observations steps](https://w3c.github.io/IntersectionObserver/#run-the-update-intersection-observations-steps)), whereas Web Animations appears to [treat the passed-in timestamp as absolute](https://drafts.csswg.org/web-animations-1/#document-timelines), performing its own relativization.
